intents.text: Add a `max_body_size` option (default `None`, meaning unlimited as today) to `Starlette`, `Router`, `Mount` and `Route`.
The application-level limit applies before routing, and a limit set on an inner route, mount or router overrides the outer one for that part of the tree, whether it raises or lowers the outer limit.
Provide a standalone ASGI middleware `RequestBodyLimitMiddleware` with the same limit behaviour that works with any ASGI application.

Count the body bytes actually received from the ASGI server (including multipart file data and encoding overhead) against the limit, so an absent or understated `Content-Length` does not let an oversized body through.
Reject a request whose declared `Content-Length` exceeds the limit with a 413 before any of the body is read.
A request that exceeds the limit gets a plain-text `413 Content Too Large` response; if the application has already started its response, no second response is sent and the body stream is stopped.
Multipart parsing closes its temporary files whenever a parse is interrupted, including when the request crosses the body limit.

Add tests for the limit on the application, router, mount and route (including an inner limit raising and lowering the outer one), the standalone middleware, the Content-Length fail-fast, the multipart case and temp-file cleanup.

constraints: Default `max_body_size=None` must keep today's unlimited behaviour.
The existing test suite must stay green.
